text: Weekly Online Quiz (Quiz/test, 30%). Respond to the quiz questions for each module related to the online video learning prompts. Students will need to access Canvas and watch the online materials in order to respond to the quiz questions.

Critical Analysis of an Aboriginal Place in Sydney (Report, 25%). Aboriginal people continue to maintain deep connections to place and Country in the Sydney region. This critical analysis requires that you learn more about a place that illuminates Aboriginal Sydneyâs unique historical, social, political and cultural life. Detail: To complete this task you must refer to the detailed assessment instructions provided on theâ¯subjectâ¯siteâ¯in Canvas.

Essay and Professional Reflection (Reflection, 45%). This task requires students to critically analyse contemporary issues and debates impacting on Indigenous Australians. Students are also required to reflect on the implications of their learning for their future profession. Detail: To complete this task you must refer to the detailed assessment instructions provided on the subject site in Canvas.

Application of communicable disease control principles: Online quiz (Quiz/test, 15%, Individual). One online quiz consisting of 5 multiple choice questions and one short answer question, delivered online at the end of Week 1. Questions will be drawn at random from a bank of questions.Â

Outbreak investigation (Case study, 40%, Individual). Students will be provided with a case scenario involving a communicable disease outbreak in a semi-closed setting and specific questions that will guide the investigation using principles of communicable disease transmission, epidemiology, and surveillance, as well as management and control of the outbreak. The students will be assessed based on their responses to addressing specific questions on outbreak assessment, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills pertinent to the case study.

Addressing the social determinants of communicable disease morbidity (Report, 45%, Individual). Students will identify a population and a communicable disease of public health significance. They will be required to critically analyse the literature to understand the specific needs and considerations in preventing or managing the communicable disease in this population. Students will write a report intended for the health department to highlight the specific issues and guide appropriate responses for preventing and managing a communicable disease in this population. In their report, they will also include reference to how the communicable disease has been managed in one other country of their choice for the same target population (similar high-risk groups within the community).
Basic statistical calculations (Case study, 40%, Individual). Students will be given a number of short answer questions that will require basic calculations and data manipulation tasks.

Conducting biostatistical analyses (Case study, 60%, Individual). Dataset(s) used in this case study is adapted from previous research and will be provided to students to analyse and respond to questions. Questions may relate to a variety of biostatistical concepts and methods. Students will need to use statistical software to conduct analyses and interpret the output. Further instructions are available on Canvas.

Online quizzes (Two) (Quiz/test, 20%, Individual). The quizzes will be linked to Modules 1 and 2, providing both preparation for participation in later modules and review of prior learning. Students are to answer a series of questions via Canvas. A selection of multiple choice questions will be given. Feedback will be included to allow students to revise the subject content for their second attempt. Questions may: relate to basic epidemiological concepts; require interpretation of supplied information; require calculations based on formulas; relate to important definitions.

Epidemiological Data Analysis (Report, 40%, Individual). A number of epidemiological datasets will be given for analysis. A series of structured, short answer questions will be given for each dataset. These questions will involve calculations, the interpretation of data and the drawing of conclusions from the data.

Critical Appraisal of a Journal Article (Report, 40%, Individual). You will continue to use a standard critical appraisal tool to assess a published research article against the critical appraisal tool.

Online Quizzes (Quiz/test, 40%). Students will complete three (3) online activities assessing the content of the weeksâ material, consisting of 10 multiple-choice questions per online activity. Students will have 30 minutes to complete each quiz (i.e. 10 multiple-choice questions). Questions not answered at time-out will not attract points. Students will receive feedback online (i.e. correct answers) and grades via Canvas.

Fieldwork Report (Report, 60%). This assessment requires you to undertake 2 to 3 semi-structured interviews with friends/family focusing upon the broad topic of âoral health and hygieneâ. Interviewees must be individuals with whom you are familiar and with whom you have an established relationship as we do not have ethical clearance to interview anyone else. The interviews will explore interviewees' behaviours, motivations, experiences, and understandings around this broad topic. This is an opportunity for you to explore and unpack a topic/area of everyday life which we all may to some extent âtake for grantedâ and not regularly discuss or share with others. Interviews should be between 15-20 minutes each. You can either take handwritten notes only during the interviews or also supplement such notes with a digital recording (so long as you have verbal consent of the interviewees). Upon completion of the interview, you will take 10 minutes to write notes to reflect upon the experience of the interview including reflection upon your own role in the process and what you consider went well/could be further strengthened/was a challenge (do please note that the longer you leave between completing the interview and undertaking this task, the less details and rich insights you are likely to remember). The semi-structured interviews need to be framed around questions that can help you explore the following areas: The interviewees' understandings of what oral hygiene/health constitutes; The regimes, practices and products used by the interviewees to maintain/improve oral hygiene/health (what they use and why they use them); The interviewees' motivations and expectations regarding their own oral hygiene/health and the oral hygiene/health of family/friends; The interviewees' perspectives and understandings around who is influential (significant others) regarding their oral hygiene/health behaviours and regimes and in what ways these significant others are influential. The 4 areas outlined above act as the overarching structure for your interview guide. However, your job is to compose 2-3 specific questions for each of the 4 areas above (8-12 questions in total). Remember, you'll also have to begin the interview by introducing yourself, the project (in very general but clear terms - do not explain or read out the details of the theme list/interview guide) and what is expected of them and you during this fieldwork experience. Keep in mind that many interviewees may never have participated in qualitative research or qualitative interviews before and do not necessarily assume they are familiar with what is involved and/or expected of them. To analyse your collected data you must undertake a basic Framework Approach analysis following the framework approach process and steps (as outlined in the Module 4.4). Do not attempt to use any other qualitative analysis approach in this assessment. Students will produce a report from the interview process and results. The report will follow a four heading structure (see Guidelines for Document Submission outlined below). Do please note: while addressing all four sections outlined below is essential to this assessment, please note the section dedicated to you providing critical reflection upon your fieldwork experience is of priority (and has been allocated largest wordcount and possible marks). Be careful to allocate sufficient word count to each section in accordance with the wordcount max provided.

Transnational Actors in Global health (Essay, 30%, Individual). Identify a transnational actor in the public health area, briefly describe its objective or mission and analyse its work and mission in the context of the Global Charter for the Publicâs Health (Word Health Organization, 2015). How well do the actorâs aims and activities fulfil the goals of the Global Charter? Which services and enablers in the Charter does the actor focus on, and are these sufficient to fulfil its objective or mission?

Government Policy Brief (Essay, 70%, Individual). Select an issue with relevance to public health on a global or regional level (beyond a single country). Prepare a brief for the Department of Health concerning strategies and investments needed based on evidence in the contemporary literature. Outline why a global response is required and why the Australian government should invest in this area. Comment on the role the Australian Government can play in addressing this issue domestically and on a global scale.

Contribution to discussion boards and online activities (Exercises, 30%, Individual). Students will provide relevant and meaningful contributions to online activities and discussions. Two discussion boards will be highlighted in the system as âthis is a marked discussionâ. For each discussion board, students must make one original submission in short essay or short answer format (about 400 words) and at least one comment on a posting by a fellow student. Integrate a recent example from a newspaper, blog or other non-academic outlet that is relevant to the topic. Explain why this topic resonated with you or how it connects to something you've encountered in your studies, community, work or other aspect of your life. Â Students are permitted to use generative AI tools for any aspect of their work, including idea generation and content creation. However, all use must be declared, naming the AI tool(s) used, explaining how they were used, and including a brief reflection on how AI contributed to the final submission. Students are responsible for ensuring that their work meets academic integrity standards and for critically evaluating all AI-generated material.

Integrated health promotion programs (Presentation, 30%, Individual). This assessment focuses on applying your understanding of the principles of integrated health promotion. This assessment consists of two components: Oral Presentation (70% of total grade) Record a 5â6 minute presentation in which you: Introduce a real-world health promotion program (you can find a list of approved topics on Canvas) Analyse how well the program aligns with the framework for integrated health promotion, including its use of strategies, stakeholder engagement, and community relevance. Evaluate the programâs strengths and limitations. Recommend specific strategies to improve the program, supported by theories and frameworks discussed in the subject. The presentation should be delivered in a professional but conversational tone. You may use slides or visuals if you wish, but this is not mandatory. Â Summary Submission (30% of total grade) Submit a written summary (max 400 words) that outlines the key points of your presentation, including references used in the form of an abstract. This must include a list of all references used for the oral presentation. Â Students may use generative AI tools for grammar checking, language improvements, and to support background research (e.g., identifying key concepts or summarising public information). AI-generated content must not be submitted as original work. All use must be declared, specifying which tools were used and how they were used. Students remain fully responsible for the academic quality, accuracy, and originality of their submissions.

Health promotion program planning (Report, 40%, Individual). Select a population and health issue from the list provided on Canvas. Develop a brief health promotion program that fits both the selected population and health behaviour using relevant concepts and theories discussed throughout the subject. Choose one of the combinations as set out on Canvas. Your program must demonstrate a clear and evidence-based rationale for all components and show how subject content has informed your decision-making. Specifically, your submission must include: Integration of Subject Activities or Discussions: Reference at least one subject activity, discussion post, or weekly task (e.g., Activity 3B: Plan an anti-smoking campaign or Activity 5A: Spectrum of interventions) that shaped your understanding or informed your program design. Briefly explain how this content influenced your approach. Annotated Program Justification Table: Include a one-page table that outlines the key components of your program. For each component, describe: The intervention or activity (or components thereof Its theoretical underpinning (linked to subject content or activities) Supporting evidence from contemporary literature (past 10 years) A rationale for its relevance to the target population and behaviour. Use the template provided. Students are permitted to use generative AI tools for any aspect of their work, including idea generation and content creation. However, all use must be declared, naming the AI tool(s) used, explaining how they were used, and including a brief reflection on how AI contributed to the final submission. Students are responsible for ensuring that their work meets academic integrity standards and for critically evaluating all AI-generated material.

Critical Evidence Brief (Presentation, 20%, Individual). Description: In this assessment, you will record a 5â6 minute video presentation reflecting on two peer-reviewed articles selected from a provided list on non-communicable disease (NCD) prevention and management. This task is designed to develop your ability to critically evaluate evidence and communicate its relevance to policy, practice, and your own personal, academic, or professional goals. Your presentation should: Briefly summarise each article, identifying its scope, key findings, and conclusions.Â Reflect on common themes, contrasting approaches, or shared challenges across the two articles Discuss the significance of these articles to youâwhy they matter in light of your interests, experiences, or career plans Clearly name the titles and authors of both articles during the recording Make sure your presentation is appropriate for a lay audience (i.e., delivered in a way that is understandable to an audience who may be less familiar with academic or medical language).Â This is an oral presentation and reflection, not a slide-based presentation. You may use props or simple visual aids to support your message, but PowerPoint or other digital slides are not permitted. If you refer to additional sources, you may upload a brief reference list in APA format alongside your video.Students must clearly name the titles and authors of both articles in the recording. If other sources are cited, a brief reference list in APA format should be submitted alongside the video.

Contribution to online discussion forums (Portfolio, 30%, Individual). Students will contribute to two online discussion forums for each of the three modules. For each module, they must post one original contribution (200â250 words) and one response to a peer (100â150 words). Posts must be written during the discussion period and submitted as originally postedâno editing is permitted. Each main contribution must include a personal reflection that connects the topic to the studentâs own experiences, values, or professional interests, and refer to relevant readings. Timely participation is essential and will be considered in marking. At the end of the session, students will choose their best two 200-word original contributions and best two 100-word responses to other students for submission to Canvas for Assessment.

Critical appraisal of policy or program (Essay, 50%, Individual). In this task, you will choose one policy or framework from the list provided and critically assess how it addresses the prevention and/or management of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) for a specific priority community. You must examine who is included or excluded, the strategies used, and the evidence base supporting them in the context of your own role as a healthcare worker, carer, or patientâeither current or future. Your essay should offer a clear, evidence-informed critique of the policyâs effectiveness and relevance, while also reflecting on its implications for your professional or personal practice. The aim is to link policy to lived experience and real-world responsibilities, showing how high-level strategies translate into everyday action and care.

Annotated bibliography (Annotated bibliography, 30%, Individual). By the end of week 1 students are to select two peer reviewed papers related to planetary health from a provided list of recent publications and submit a 300 word commentary on each paper. Students are to provide a summary of the work (e.g. background of the authors, scope, main argument and conclusions), to critically review the credibility of the evidence and to comment on how this work helped them (or not) better understand planetary health issues.

Essay (Essay, 70%, Individual). Students will be required to submit a 2,000-word essay on a specific public health issue related to climate change in a selected country of their choice with the aim to improve planetary and public health under a changing climate. Students are to propose a multi-faceted, interdisciplinary and comprehensive solution, including some components from policy and behaviour change.

Introductory regression analysis (Report, 25%). You will be given one dataset that you will need to read in to a software package (Stata). You will be asked to complete some basic descriptive analyses that develop the methods learnt in 090012 Fundamentals of Biostatistics as well as fitting linear and multiple linear regression models. You will be required to interpret the results of the analyses by writing simple, succinct summaries.

Statistical analysis of continuous and binary data (Report, 35%). You will be given one dataset to analyse. You will be given a number of short-answer questions that will require you to conduct linear or logistic regression analyses as appropriate, determine model fit, carry out appropriate diagnostics, and build appropriate statistical models. You will need to provide an interpretation of the models that can be read by someone not trained in biostatistics. You will need to justify your decisions about the statistical analyses and approaches that you have chosen. You will need to provide appropriate computer code, graphics, and summaries of your analyses in your answers.

Consulting report (Report, 40%). You will be given an epidemiological problem from a client (e.g. a public health or clinical researcher) and a dataset that you will need to analyse. The analysis will involve time-to-event data. The client, who is not trained in biostatistics, has requested that you provide her with an easily understood statistical report with a separate technical appendix. You have been asked to address the following in your report: Methods: you will need to describe and justify the methods you have chosen for analysis, your approach to model building, and any regression diagnostics and checks of model fit that you have undertaken. Results: you will need to summarise the results of your analyses, paying particular attention to providing a clearly written interpretation of your final regression model that can be understood by someone not trained in biostatistics. Strengths and limitations: You will need to discuss any strengths and limitations of your approach and of the regression model. You will need to provide appropriate computer code, graphics, and summaries of your analyses in the technical appendix.

Short Answers (Exercises, 15%, Individual). In this assessment task, you will be required to answer 5 short answer questions in a research scenario. In each question, you will be asked to calculate or comment on epidemiological aspects of the scenario. This assessment task will be provided to you via Canvas.

Critical review (Essay, 35%, Individual). In this assessment task you will be provided with two journal articles, one of which will be a randomised controlled trial and the other an observational study. You will be required to critically appraise the journal articles. You will need to assess the methodological quality of the studies and to determine the extent to which a study has addressed the possibility of bias in their design, conduct and analysis.

Study design (Case study, 50%, Individual). This assessment is designed to provide students with a practical example of how to design an appropriate study to answer a typical public health research question. The activity facilitates an understanding of how different research approaches can be employed to explore issues in health. Task: In this assessment task, you will be provided with a scenario which includes the background and objective of a research study. Your task will be to describe how you would undertake a study to address the objective using a number of different study designs. The scenario and specific study designs to be considered will be provided via Canvas.

Online participation (Exercises, 5%, Individual). Students are asked to create an introductory video and upload it to the Introduction to Peers discussion board on Canvas. The purpose of this video is to help students get acquainted with their peers, and to connect with potential partners for the term project. You may include your name, your past degrees, relevant courses taken, and work experiences, why you are taking this course, what you wish to learn, and/or anything else you would like to share, recognizing that everyone enrolled in this course will be able to watch your video. Please limit your video to one minute. Students should review the videos of your peers and use the discussion board to connect with potential partners for the term project. Please notify me once you have formed a team or if you have difficulty with this.

Online weekly quiz (Quiz/test, 30%, Individual). There will be questions embedded in the module content. Students must complete the questions on an individual basis during the week in which the module is to be completed. The quiz provides students with feedback on their progress and understanding of the key analytical concepts presented to date. 5% per weekly quiz x 6 weeks.

Group project (Project, 35%, Group, group and individually assessed). The term project is a group project plan (2%), group presentation video (28%) with peer assessment (5%). This project must be completed with one or more partners, preferably 3-4 members in total. You can connect with potential partners on the Introduction to Peers discussion board in the first week. You will have the same partner(s) throughout the term project. Please notify me once you have formed a team. If you encounter difficulties, I will take the responsibility of assigning team members. I reserve the right to assign different grades within a team in case of unequal contributions. Further details of the presentation and peer assessment will be provided on Canvas.

Report on market failure in health care (Report, 30%, Individual). Students write a report that focuses on one part of health production or the health care sector of their choice. Students identify potential sources of market failure and examine how these affect the efficiency and/or equity of their chosen. Finally, students must describe a government intervention that addresses at least one of the identified market failures and reflect on the strengths and weaknesses of the intervention.

subject_name: Improving Safety and Quality in Healthcare
text: Complaints Management (Case study, 40%, Individual). You are given a scenario, in which you are a general manager of a health service, tasked with responding to a letter of complaint.Â Detailed information about the scenario, including the complaint letter, is provided in Canvas. Complete the following steps: Read the letter of complaint from the family. Compose and submit a formal letter of response to the author/s of the letter, in your capacity as general manager.Â Note the following important instructions: Your response should reflect that you have already completed an investigation into the issues raised, and have communicated with the complainant/s, in any way that you think is required. Your response shouldÂ clearly indicate that you found evidence to support many of the issues raised in the letter (i.e. they were substantiated ), but for at least 2 issues , you were not able to find sufficient evidence to support the issues as presented. You can choose which issues were substantiated and which ones lacked evidence.

subject_name: Improving Safety and Quality in Healthcare
text: Organisation of Safety and Quality Improvement Seminars (Presentation, 60%, Individual). Scenario: You are a staff member at Greenview Hospital (or you can choose another health or social care facility, e.g. residential aged care home, community health centre, primary care clinic). Your manager has asked you to share what you've been learning in this subject with your colleagues, by delivering a short seminar. They are interested in the topic of safety culture, and want to know if it is the same thing as cultural safety or something different. Your manager wants you to explain what these terms mean, and how they can be improved in your service. Your submission for this assessment is in two parts . Part A: Seminar presentation (script only) You decide to write a short presentation, based on content you have been taught in this subject, and additional research evidence. Detailed information about what is required in your script is provided in Canvas. Submit aÂ 2500-word Microsoft Word document of your presentation script (what you say during the presentation), including in-text citations and a full reference list.Â Â Part B: Self-reflection (short video recording) After preparing your presentation, you consider how you might persuade colleagues to come to your seminar. You decide to role model critical self-reflexivity about: a) what you have learnt about safety culture and cultural safety, and b) how your learnings will influence your current or future professional practice. SubmitÂ a 3-4Â minute self-reflection video, that you would share with colleagues. No referencing is required in this video.

Recognising leadership (Essay, 15%, Individual). Choose a person you believe to be an effective leader from a movie, book, popular culture, or modern history (ie the last 100 years) and analyse what contributed or contributes to their effectiveness using one or more of the leadership theories we review as part of this subject.

Leadership and followership (Essay, 35%, Individual). Leadership is not possible without followership. What does followership mean and what does it entail? Why is it important in health or social care to consider followership? What particular difficulties (if any) do you think leaders in health or social care face in attracting and keeping followers and in getting them to do what is required to meet organisational goals?

Crisis leadership (Case study, 50%, Individual). Crises bring to the fore both the success and failures of leaders and leadership at all levels of society, and across sectors. What are the ethical issues which arise from the way crises are handled by leaders including in health or social care systems? Students will be supplied with a case study to critically analyse as part of this assessment.

What's the problem? (Essay, 25%, Individual). STEP 1 : Choose one of the following health-related innovations, which have been presented as solutions to particular problems in health: Activity-tracking apps (and associated wearable devices) - e.g. Fitbits, Apple Watch, etc. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based chatbots for digital mental health STEP 2 : Research the policies, peer-reviewed academic literature, and (credible) news media around these innovations, to critically analyse how these innovations have been developed, by whom, and to identify what assumptions they include, about the problem/s that they are designed to solve. Drawing on your research, answer the following 7 questions in a short answer essay format. You can refer to Australian and international examples in your answers. What is the âproblemâ that is this innovation is represented as addressing? There may be multiple problems, if so, mention them all, but pick one to discuss in the rest of your report. What assumptions are made about the problem? (E.g. how the problem has come about, whose behaviour needs to change, what the barriers to solving the problem have been in the past, etc.) Who has been involved in developing, presenting and implementing this innovation, and who was not included? What sources did they draw on? (Private enterprise? Researchers? NGOs? Professional groups? Consumers? Advocacy groups?) Are there other ways of describing âthe problemâ, as described in your answer to question 2? For instance, are there other explanations for how the problem has come about? What are some of the possible consequences of implementing this innovation? (E.g. how might it impact on the way we talk about these issues, how does it portray people, how does it affect how people see themselves, how might it affect how people live their lives?) How has this innovation been implemented, disseminated (or marketed), and what are some alternative approaches to the problem? Reflecting on the research and analysis you have just completed, what is something you have learnt or reconsidered about the innovation you have chosen? (150 words) IMPORTANT : Your submission should also include a brief introductory statement to tell the reader which innovation you are investigating. TIPS: These questions are based on the WPR framework by Carol Bacchi , introduced in Week 1. You should review that module for resources and activities to understand the rationale and intent of each of the questions. The questions should be incorporated as headings. Your responses to each of the questions should be supported by references to relevant policies, government or NGO reports, peer-reviewed academic literature, and, where appropriate, from credible news media (e.g. The Conversation).

A toolkit for human-centred design (Presentation, 30%, Individual). SCENARIO You are a consultant who has been invited to give a presentation to a group of senior managers at a health and/or social care organisation. This presentation is an opportunity to win a contract to: deliver a set of resources and a program of training to upskill the organisation on desgining human-centred innovations. Review the project brief provided on Canvas for more details about the organisation and their particular needs. TASK You are asked to submit a presentation consisting of a maximum of 12 Powerpoint slides (in PDF format) with a 1500 word (max) âscriptâ including the following: A cover slide to introduce yourself and the topic you will be discussing [1 slide] Why human-centred design (HCD) is important for innovation in healthcare [1 slide] Key principles of HCD [1 slide] A description of what a design âprocess' looks like [2-4 slides] A mini sample âtoolkitâ of four HCD methods/tools that you recommend for their organisation (and explain why you believe these to be suitable for them. These methods/tools should assist innovators to: i) identify the needs and experiences of key users and stakeholders in the design process, and ii) prototype and test solutions within the context of the services that the organisation provides. [2-4 slides] A hypothetical example of how the service might use two of the HCD methods/tools identified to design an innovative solution, with the aim of "improving communication between consumers and service providers within the organisation" . A final slide with key takeaway messages.

An organisational guide to innovation (Report, 45%, Individual). SCENARIO The Head of Innovation at Uniting was happy with the presentation that you delivered in Assessment 2, and has engaged your consultancy to provide organisational training on human-centred design. As part of this contract, she has also asked for a guide on how to support human-centred design and design thinking within their organisation. In particular, she is interested in how the organisation can foster innovative thinking (mindsets) and systematically support the development and spread of innovations throughout the organisation. She is particularly interested in the challenge of engaging their clinical staff in innovation. To develop this guide, you should draw on what you have learnt in this subject, about approaches to fostering innovation within organisations, including: the organisational factors that support the development and spread of innovative practices in a complex health and social service organisation; and the regulatory frameworks, policies, standards and risks (e.g. privacy, confidentiality, equity, accountability/governance, patient safety) that need to be taken into consideration when designing and implementing innovations in that particular organisation. TASK You should submit a 2000 word report, supported by the research literature, which should include the following sections: a) Introduction â to explain what innovation is; why innovation is important in health and social care and for Uniting in particular; why human-centred design is an important approach for innovation; and the purpose of this document. b) Workplace culture c) Leadership and governance d) Infrastructures of innovation e) Ethics, risks, regulations and standards f) A list of key recommendations TIPS We expect you to demonstrate an understanding of the concepts taught in this subject. Start with the course-provided readings when doing your research. The mention of organisational training in the scenario is just for background information, it is not part of this assessment.

Critical Reflection (Reflection, 20%). Compose a critical reflection (500 words excluding reference list) on your personal experience of being involved in a workplace change initiative. Consider carefully, the definition of a " workplace change initiative" to demonstrate your understanding of an appropriate scenario. You are asked to link your reflection to your knowledge of multi-facets of change supported by content covered in Week 1and appropriate research evidence to critique the experience. You can use the critical reflection writing guide (below) to structure your critical reflection. Use the resources below to assist you with the structure of your assessment and your critical reflection. Please note it acts as a guide only. â Watch this helpful short video on critical reflection. Links to an external site. In addition to the critical reflection writing guide below, you may want to look at Acawriter , a tool that helps develop your academic and reflective writing by providing instant, automatic feedback on your drafts, 24/7.

Video and Essay (Essay, 40%). Read this case study describing a situation (scenario) in which you assume the role of a Consultant Change Manager. Note: You will use this scenario for Assessment 2 and 3. This assessment (Assessment 2) includes 2 parts: A âcase for changeâ pitch ( video 2-3 minutes), presented to Executives and other key stakeholders to persuade and request allocation of funding for a future implementation of recommended change initiatives An essay (1000 words), expanding on details within the pitch, to justify the case for change and detail the approach youâre recommending for the recommended change initiative Step One In additional to Executives, determine the key stakeholder group you will pitch to (address) relevant to the scenario. Give context to this consideration within both parts of the assessment. Step Two Develop a video (2-3 minutes) of yourself in your role (see case study scenario) communicating the need for change and the vision for change, to your chosen stakeholder group and the Executive. This video requires you to pitch why the change is important. The aim is to get the stakeholders on board with the need for change and the change initiative. Step Three Compose an essay justifying what was said in your video, using the literature on leadership and change management (with references) (1000 words excluding reference list). More specifically it should contain: an introduction clearly outlining the problem you are trying to solve and why it is important to solve the problem (case for change) (supported by critical analysis of literature) and the rationale for the change initiative/project (supported by literature), clearly articulating what success should look like (supported by literature) the rationale will include the strategic alignment of the change initiative to service/organisation plans justify the methodology (approach) (based on critical analysis of literature) you will use to find out what is causing the problem and why it needs to be addressed How will you find out what the main factors are that will enable or hinder the change initiative and identify what you anticipate these might be identify the key stakeholders who will influence and/or be impacted by the change initiative justify (based on critical analysis of literature) the change model you think is the most appropriate given the type of change and the context in which it needs to occur justify (based on critical analysis of literature) the leadership/management style(s) you think is most appropriate in this context to engage people in the change proposed duration of the change initiative Â Case study Download your case study here .

Action Plan for a Change Initiative (Report, 40%). Continuing your role outlined in the casestudy scenario from Assessment 2, as the Consultant Change Manager you are asked to produce an Implementation and Evaluation Action Plan (for the change initiative pitched in Assessment 2) that describes the approach, how and what actions, you will take to implement and evaluate the proposed change (what, how and why). Apply theories of change to develop your Implementation and Evaluation Action Plan. Critically appraise the approach to working with stakeholders, conducting the change, and initiating, sustaining and measuring benefit. Â Your plan will include the methodology that you will use to evaluate whether the change initiative activities have been implemented as intended and how the evaluation findings will be used to ensure ongoing success of the implemented change initiative. You might use applicable core details from Assessment 2, as a foundation on which to build a more detailed and informative Implementation and Evaluation Action Plan . Use the template provided to guide required inclusions in line with the scenario provided in the case study .

Personal improvement project proposal (Report, 20%, Individual). Create a simple plan to take the first steps towards improving one aspect of your own life over the course of the following five weeks in this subject. To make this achievable, you should choose something that occurs regularly and frequently (e.g. daily) and is within your control to change, such as your own behaviour. (TIP: keep it simple and focused.) Examples in your personal life may be: to be more physically active, set aside time for self-care, get more sleep, change your diet, reduce alcohol consumption, etc. Examples in your professional life may be: to better manage your emails, to increase your study time, to leave work on time more frequently, etc. In this assessment, you should apply the principles learnt in Week 1 to put together a short proposal. Follow the instructions below on how to structure this proposal and what to include. 1. Answer the following questions, using the headings (those in bold) in your submission. You should consider the points below the headings when answering the questions. Write in first person, and support your points with the literature where you can. a. What is the problem about, and what might you be able to do about it? How would you describe the problem to someone else? What information do you have, to show that this is something that needs to be improved? Is there information available in the research literature about other peopleâs experiences of this issue? b. What are some actions (interventions) you could feasibly trial to address this problem now? Why do you think they might help? What might prevent you from taking those actions? What might help? If you have tried to address this problem before, your reflections on that process would be highly relevant and useful here. Is there information in the research literature about what interventions have been trialled by others, and their enablers and barriers? Which of these interventions would you trial first, and why? c. How are you going to know that you have made an improvement? What outcome measure/s could you record to understand what the current situation is so that you will know if it has changed in the future (improvement)? Note: before you change anything, you should first record this data for a period of time, as a baseline measure. What measure/s could you record to keep track of the processes that affect your outcomes? What measure/s could you record to keep track of what other important aspects of your life might be impacted by your project? (These are known as balancing measures.) d. What might be a realistic improvement to aim for in five weeks? Can you find information in the research literature to help you to determine what can be achieved, realistically, in five weeks? e. What is your proposed aims statement? Present your aims statement here, based on your answers to the above questions. Refer to the aims statement activity in Module 1 for support. 2. Next, create a record-keeping and reflection journal (not to submit), where you will record the following information: your data (what you choose to measure) recorded at regular intervals throughout weeks 2 to 6 the interventions that you have actioned ongoing and regular reflections on your project any modifications you have made to your plan. This journal can be kept whatever way suits you best - digitally (e.g. a spreadsheet) or on paper. Your records in this journal will be necessary to complete assessments 2 and 3. You do not submit this journal.

Research Report (Written submission, 35%, Individual). You will follow a tutorial in Canvas, with opportunities to check your progress at each step.

Your analysis should follow three key phases: Business Context and Stakeholder Analysis, Data Analysis and Insights and Future Analysis Plan. This report serves as a foundation for Assessment Task 3, where you will implement your proposed advanced analytics approach.

Data Story Video Presentation (Presentation, 40%, Individual). In-class Exercises (Quiz/test, 30%, Individual). During each seminar, you will be required to complete previously unseen accounting exercises. These exercises require you to apply the material that you have read and reflected upon prior to attending class. The questions will be a mix of theory, practical and numeric-based questions. Your answers to these questions will be collected randomly five times throughout the session.

Case Study using Computer Accounting Software (Case study, 20%, Individual). This assessment will develop your practical accounting skills and allow you to practice performing real world transactions using mainstream accounting software. You will be required to utilise a Computer Accounting Program to develop a chart of accounts, process business transactions and generate financial reports.

Final Exam (Examination, 50%, Individual). The exam tests your ability to evaluate a firmâs activities using financial information and to apply basic cost and management accounting concepts to derive product costs and generate financial information with recommendations to decision-makers. These skills are essential for professionals in the work environment and the exam tests your ability to integrate technical and professional accounting skills in various contexts. The questions in the exam include authentic cases and scenarios which are encountered in real-world business.

In-class Tests (Examination, 20%, Individual). Starting from week 3 an in-class topic test will be conducted at the start of some lecture/seminar session. There will be a total of 4 in-class tests. Students should attend and undertake all in-class tests; however, assessment marks will be awarded based on each student's best 3 topic test results. This item covers objectives 1,2 and 3 as well as their integration with the other objectives.

Simulated Project (Project, 30%, Group, group and individually assessed). Students will be required to form groups of 3-4 and participate in a simulated project management process. Each group will complete project meetings and will be required to make project management decisions based on the specific information provided to each group. Students will be required to utilise project management software to assist in planning and monitoring the simulated project. The simulated project will begin in Week 4 and groups will be required to submit two Project Reports during the semester. The reports should be submitted through the assignment section of Canvas. Time will be allocated in-class for project work and group meetings however groups are likely to require additional time outside of class for group meetings. From week 4, detailed assignment specifications including the marking rubrics will be available on Canvas. Academic integrity: This assessment is about the team's approach to solving a given problem(s) and the work should be the team's own words. All submissions will be processed through Turnitin for similarity checking. Any references used in preparing your group reports should be appropriately referenced using the APA 7 referencing standard. The UTS Library provides an APA 7 referencing guide. Late submission policy: Any assessment task submitted after the due date and time will be either: penalised by way of loss of marks. 10 per cent (10%) of the total marks for the assessment task will be deducted per day for assessment tasks submitted after the due date. A day is defined as a 24-hour period or part thereof following the published due date and time of the assignment, and rejected and not marked if the assessment is submitted more than 5 calendar days after the stated submission date unless a formal extension of time has been granted by the Subject Coordinator. Approved extensions cannot be made without a request for extension sent directly to the coordinator via email to maria.ossimitz@uts.edu.au (for extensions of one week or less) or via an application for special consideration (for extensions of more than one week, within the UTS time frames for submission). Final Exam (Examination, 50%, Individual). The final exam, which will be 'centrally conducted', will address all learning objectives. The final exam will require students to apply and integrate concepts and knowledge from the topics covered throughout the semester. The exam will include a variety of question types (i.e. multiple-choice, multiple answers, fill the blank) as well as short answer questions and a case study.

Class problems (Exercises, 30%, Group, group assessed). Each week in tutorial sessions, you will work in assigned groups to solve financial analytics problems using real-world datasets. Your group will analyse business scenarios, apply appropriate analytical techniques, and present your findings to the class. Activities will vary in focus, covering different aspects of financial analytics including data preparation, analysis, visualisation, and communication of insights. This progressive assessment helps you develop practical experience in collaborative problem-solving while building your financial analytics toolkit. This assessment assures the following course intended learning outcomes: Collaborate with colleagues and a range of stakeholders to deliver negotiated business outcomes

Balanced Scorecard Case Study (Case study, 40%, Individual). You are an analyst at a large Australian firm, recently appointed to a committee tasked with developing a balanced scorecard that aligns with the firm's strategic vision and operational goals. The firm aims to integrate comprehensive performance metrics beyond traditional financial indicators to include non-financial metrics that reflect the organisation's commitment to social responsibility, environmental sustainability and reconciliation action. This assessment consists of two parts: the Financial Analysis Dashboard (15%) and the KPI development plan (25%). Your first task is to analyse a data file provided to you. This data file contains financial information that reflects the firm's past and current financial performance. Beyond financial metrics, the firm recognises the importance of including non-financial metrics in the balanced scorecard to achieve a holistic view of performance. You are to develop a plan for the KPIs that the firm should measure as part of this balanced scorecard. This assessment assures the following course intended learning outcomes: Communicate complex data-informed decisions clearly in written, verbal and visual form to a range of business stakeholders Critically reflect on the rights to consent, privacy, data sovereignty and self determination to work ethically with and for Indigenous Australians as business analytics professionals

Final Exam (Examination, 30%, Individual). You will complete a final exam in a computer lab. You will be examined on theoretical knowledge and practical skills developed in the subject. The exam is a closed book exam. You will be required to analyse datasets, utilise software such as Tableau to create visualisations, and answer written theoretical questions on financial concepts.

In-class activities (Quiz, 30%, Individual). Throughout the session, students will complete four individual in-class analytics activities during scheduled workshop sessions. Each activity is designed to assess the application of analytical techniques, including data visualisation, to a business scenario using relevant tools and datasets. Each activity is equally weighted, and the best three out of four activities will be used to calculate the final mark for this assessment (each contributing 10%), resulting in a total weighting of 30%. These activities are completed in a controlled environment to ensure independent work and are designed to build foundational capability across the analytics workflow, including data preparation, analysis,visualisation, and interpretation. The âbest threeâ approach promotes fairness and accommodates variability in student performance across the semester.

Business Analytics Report (Written submission, 30%, Group, group assessed). In this assessment, students will work in groups to analyse a business scenario and dataset. The task focuses on conducting exploratory and descriptive analysis to understand the business context and data landscape. Students will apply multiple analytical approaches to explore the data, compare key findings, and generate insights to inform business decision-making. The analysis should be supported by appropriate use of analytical techniques and data visualisation. This report serves as a foundation for Assessment 3, where students will independently implement and extend advanced analytics approaches based on insights developed in this assessment.

Data Story Video Presentation (Presentation, 40%, Individual). Â You will build on insights developed in Assessment 2 to independently implement your proposed advanced analytics approach and create a professional pre-recorded presentation. Â Your presentation should show a progression from your initial analysis, highlighting how the advanced methods provide deeper or different insights into the business problem. Your presentation should be clear, appropriate for your audience, and include clear and actionable recommendations. It should include insights from your advanced analytical methods and the use of data visualisations to support your narrative. In this assessment, you will also receive feedback on your academic language level. If your language is below the required standard, you will be invited to attend further language support.

The first part of each class will be dedicated to analysing the issues presented in the case. Written report (Report, 30%, Group, group assessed). In-class case study (Case study, 40%, Individual). In the lead up to the final class, you will receive a case study focusing on an organisation's initial plans to conduct a research project. You will be required to analyse the organisation's preliminary data collection methods and governance structures. You will need to familiarise yourself with relevant ethical principles and regulations that may be relevant to the data collection task. You will also need to study the AIATSIS Code of Ethics and Indigenous data sovereignty principles.

Case Study Presentation (Individual) (Presentation, 25%). Students will use relevant data to inform a presentation on a current economic issue. Students are required to produce a visual representation of appropriate economic models along with a basic economic analysis to provide an insight into the economic issue in question. Students will also compare the gap that exists between the Indigenous and non-Indigenous Australians, paying attention to the potential causal factors.

Report (Individual) (Report, 50%). This assessment requires students to produce a report of a real-life problem that is relevant to their business, organisation or industry. Students will use their knowledge of economic tools and analysis gained in this subject to provide the appropriate solution or managerial strategy.

This assessment requires students to identify a current macroeconomic issue sourced from a media article and produce an independent economic analysis of its impact on business or the business environment. Students are expected to integrate theory with the content described in the media article.

Portfolio (Portfolio, 40%, Individual). This assessment consists of two distinct tasks: online problem sets (20%) and a news analysis (20%). These problem sets focus on theoretical and real-world scenarios to which students must apply their analytical skills and understanding of economic influences on business. They consist of a combination of multiple-choice and numerical questions.

Final Exam (Final exam, 60%, Individual). The exam will consist of multiple choice, short answer, and extended response questions. Longer response questions will require you to apply economic theory to real-life scenarios and communicate economic analysis to various audiences. This assessment will be assessed for English language proficiency. You will be directed to further language support after the completion of this subject if your language is below the required standard.

Case Analysis (Written submission, 30%, Individual). In this assessment, you will conduct an industry analysis using an Australian company as a case study. Present the analysis in a report, which should include a company and industry background overview, an analysis of industry performance against benchmarks, an analysis of company performance relative to the industry, an analysis of demand and supply factors affecting industry profitability, the application of appropriate analytical frameworks and a clear presentation of relevant statistics and data.

Business Analytics Simulation (Project, 30%, Individual). As a data analyst, analyse a provided dataset through exploratory and descriptive analysis of the business context and data structure, statistical testing and regression modelling to identify key market drivers, development of data-driven predictions and business recommendations, and clear communication of insights to support decision-making.

In this assignment, you will analyse real-world data from a specific market to explore trends and identify demand and/or supply shiftsÂ over time. The overall mark for this assessment will be based on both the report and the Q&A session. This assessment assures the following course intended learning outcomes for the Master of Business Analytics: Evaluate the assumptions implicit in data and apply analytical techniques to create innovative business solutions (1.1); Integrate advanced data analysis techniques with business practices to deliver new insights that drive effective decision-making in local and international contexts (4.1).

Your presentation should examine the performance of both the company and its industry relative to relevant benchmarks and analyse the demand and supply factors affecting the industry's current and future profitability. You are expected to apply appropriate analytical frameworks and support your analysis with relevant statistics, presenting data clearly and effectively.

You will start by conducting an exploratory and descriptive analysis to understand the business context and structure of the data. Then, using linear regression, you will identify key factors driving the target outcome and generate predictions based on different business variables. You will use these insights to provide actionable, data-driven recommendations to support informed decision-making within the relevant business context.

Your work will culminate in a professional report detailing your analysis and recommendation.

subject_name: Marketing in the Age of Technology
text: Competing in the Marketplace (Individual) (Project, 30%). Part 1 This assessment task focuses on the current health of your company. To assess this health, marketing managers often employ the 5C framework, which describes the company, collaborators, customers, competitors and the overall climate in which the company operates. In this task, you will take stock of the 5Cs of your company and describe possible trajectories for them. You will identify the value that your company seeks to offer its customers and critically evaluate the 5Cs against this proposed value. You will consider how indigenous cultures and contexts manifest themselves in each of the 5Cs. Part 2 This assessment task focuses on identifying and evaluating the sources of competitive advantage for your company. To assess these sources, marketing managers often employ the VRIO framework, which evaluates whether particular resources or capabilities are valuable, rare, costly to imitate and organized to create value. In this task, you will focus on the resources and capabilities of your company as identified in assessment 1a and beyond (as for example discussed in module 2). You will pick one of the resources or capabilities which you deem most likely to create competitive advantage and evaluate this resource or capability according to the VRIO framework.

subject_name: Marketing in the Age of Technology
text: Developing a Marketing Strategy to Create Brand Value (Individual) (Report, 40%). This assessment task focuses on developing a marketing strategy to create brand value. Brand value is often one of the intangible sources of sustained competitive advantage and it requires long-term strategic thinking as it involves building associations in consumersâ minds and stable relationships. In this task, students will develop a marketing strategy for the offering they considered in assignment1 Part 1 and 2. Based on the current context of their company (the 5Cs as identified in assignment 1 Part 1) the task is to propose several steps to make the brand a source of sustainable advantage (as discussed also in assignment 1 Part 2). Students will reflect on the implications of their proposed strategy for their companyâs Indigenous stakeholders.

text: Measuring Success Video (Individual) (Presentation, 30%). This assessment task focuses on measuring the success of a marketing strategy. To assess this success, marketing managers often use different metrics which themselves are based on different data sources. The value of these metrics depends on how well they are connected to the marketing strategy as well as on the quality of the data they are based upon. In this task, you will focus on a particular point of the consumer journey. You will reflect on a companyâs existing data and market research ability to measure the strategyâs success at this point.

Research Problem and Data source (Project, 15%, Individual). Describe the company you have chosen to analyse with a focus on its business problem, the research questions you will explore, and the data sources you will use.

Application of Analytics (Project, 50%, Individual). This assessment consists of two parts: Data Visualisation and Storytelling (20%) andÂ Interpretation of Analytical Results (30%). You will investigate variables of their interest and find any interesting observations or patterns and create a slide deck that represents and explore your data. Then, you will run analyses to generate insights into your business problem and research questions. You will create a slide deck which includes tables or charts showing how your data helps answer your research questions, and you will identify valuable customers or segments.Â

Video Presentation (Presentation, 35%, Individual). In this assessment, you will develop recommendations based on the findings which address the business issue. Submit a short video to deliver research findings and recommendations.

Advertising Certificates (Project, 10%, Individual). You will be tasked with earning two free, external certifications from known, prominent external digital marketing and emerging technology providers. The first certification will focus on a traditional advertising method, while the second certification will focus on a social media advertising method; with both certifications relying on the use of emerging technologies in their training. Overall, these certifications help train you on how to apply their digital marketing and emerging technology learning on real-world platforms that you are likely to employ in the near-future. Further, these certifications are designed to enhance your understanding of digital marketing with an emphasis on a specific technology, The primary objective of this task is to provide you "hands-on" experience with cutting-edge, practical digital marketing tools through free external training from known providers. The secondary objective of this task is for you to earn the two certifications, sought out by job providers, in order to improve your job and/or job prospects.Â The subject coordinator will provide a list of potential certifications for you to complete for the semester.Â You should expect each certification course to take between 2-5 hours to complete, depending on which certificate you select. Further, you should expect the requirements for the certification completion for the subject to be freeÂ (although there may be an optional option for you to pay to obtain an official certificate, which will not be required for the subject).Â Finally, the online learning systems for the two certificates provide evidence when you complete the online courses and earns certificates, so it will be relatively straightforward for you to demonstrate completion of the training and evidence of obtaining the certificate.

Customer and Company Evaluation (Presentation, 30%, Group, group and individually assessed). You will be tasked with a group project analysing a company's current use of digital marketing and emerging technologyÂ in line with the material covered in the subject prior to the assessment due date. You will be provided with a template for how to structure your presentation to ensure guidance for how to fit material within the time limit.

Digital Marketing and Emerging Technology Report (Report, 60%, Individual). This assessment tests your knowledge of course material from the entire session in a task that forces you to demonstrate comprehension and an ability to apply the course material in the real-world. You will be tasked with creating a digital marketing plan for a company that covers the following topics: Improvement recommendations for the company's digital marketing and emergent technologies, based on an understanding of the company's customers, competitors, company, and marketing goalÂ Implementation of the proposed recommendations,Â which includes specific examples, a required budget, action plans and timelines Business outcome assessments to demonstrate how the recommendations will enhance the value of the company Each student is required to write the report individually. In contrast to assessment #2, you are tasked to come up with an entire plan on your own that best suits the company (compared to being given the plan to analyse). You will be provided a template for how to structure their reports to ensure guidance for how to fit material within the word limit. Assessments will examine the validity and the justifications for the recommendations, implementation, and business outcomes, in line with class materials, real-world practicality, and level of specifics provided. Further, you are expected to employ class material from throughout the session in the development of the project; and the use of class material will be part of the task assessment. Â Â Â

Case Study (Written submission, 35%, Individual). The task involves analyzing a case. To prepare for this assessment, workshops will be held where you will analyse case studies. The assessment is designed to develop critical thinking skills through the application of value proposition concepts.Â This assessment will assess critical thinking skills and their ability to apply marketing theories to real-world business problems.Â
